object_description: two structures fanning around the break area, a compact six-storey school over a buried hall
design_condition: two structures span the break area in a fan-like manner, the school stacking six floors as a compact volume while the hall is largely below ground founded on the existing rock

positive: The authors developed an independent and differentiated urban approach
Two structures span the break area in a fan-like manner
The school develops over six floors as a compact building volume
The hall is mostly below ground and founded over the existing rock
The striking buildings have a clear structure, which is also the theme of the facades
Red recycled concrete facades are differentiated by fine nuances in the lintels and the sun protection
An additional vertical path runs through the building besides the escape stairwells
The internal access figure develops via alternating, almost playful staircases
Spatially precisely placed supports accompany the staircases in an exciting way
The hall takes up the support geometry in its facade with fine, almost point-like pillars
The strict architecture is characterised by a wealth of differentiated details and subtleties
The authors succeed in creating a child-friendly atmosphere
The surroundings develop finger-like as a built plateau towards the edge
This creates a level as a platform for the school with garden, playing field, break area and pitch
Each floor develops different spatial situations
The organisation of the double sports hall is formulated simply and clearly
The quality lies in the surprising urban setting of the volumes
The colour scheme and sophisticated details do justice to the austerity of the architecture
negative: The proximity of the school to the neighbouring residential buildings appears somewhat forced
Moving further from the existing building would be an advantage, not just for building law reasons
Filling in the topography is sometimes seen as not very natural at the slope edge
The generosity of the outdoor space can only partially do justice to the location
A harmonious atmosphere is missing especially on the large hard surfaces
The connection to the surrounding area remains somewhat schematic
The ground floor multi-purpose room is somewhat difficult to access
The proportions of the group rooms are not always convincing
Fire protection questions on the floor-by-floor separation of the staircases remain unanswered
The economic requirements are barely met
The sustainability targets have been exceeded
The neglected system separation and identifiable thermal bridges are criticised
Questions remain about fire protection and the constructive implementation
